certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Government of India, all step bolts utilized on structural steel masts and transmission towers must conform to IS 10238 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling uncertified step bolts in the Indian market is a statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy industrial steel fasteners.
requirements: Every step bolt package or batch must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

For climbing safety reasons, the maximum total weight of a person—including their personal climbing tools, nuts, tackles, and gear—using these step bolts to ascend must not exceed 150 kg (or 120 kg in early standard drafts).
Each individual step bolt must be packaged and supplied complete with exactly two matching hexagon nuts.
The step bolt must belong to Product Grade C as specified in IS 1367 (Part 2), and satisfy property class 4.6 as specified in IS 1367 (Part 3).
The hexagon nuts supplied with the step bolts must belong to property class 5 and comply with IS 14394.
The accompanying plain washers must be Type A punched washers conforming to IS 2016, but feature a modified heavy-duty thickness of 5 ± 1 mm.

The step bolt must feature M16-6g screw threads complying with IS 4218. The thread pitch must be P = 2 mm, with a 2x45° end chamfer, and all edges must be smooth with zero sharp corners to prevent worker injury.
Permissible surface discontinuities of the step bolts must comply with the strict quality limits of IS 1367 (Part 9/Sec 2).

The finished step bolts must be hot-dip galvanized in accordance with IS 1367 (Part 13), and the washers galvanized per IS 4759. All dimensional limits specified in the standard apply to the product before galvanizing is executed.

Immediately after galvanizing, the hot-dip galvanized bolts, nuts, and washers must be passivated by dipping in a 0.15 percent solution of sodium dichromate with 0.5 percent concentrated sulphuric acid maintained at a temperature above 32°C to prevent wet storage strain (white rust).

To verify climbing safety, the step bolt must be tightly fixed to a structural member via a 16 mm drilled hole with the nuts tightened to the end of the threads, as illustrated in Fig. 2. The assembly must be subjected to a cantilever proof load of 150 kg (specified as 120 kg in some earlier prints) applied for 10 seconds. After unloading and re-applying the load for another 10 seconds, there must be no permanent set observed at the designated measurement point, subject to a measurement error tolerance of 30 µm.
Sampling, inspection, and acceptance criteria must conform to the standard procedures of IS 1367 (Part 17).
The step bolts must be designated by size, length, standard number, and the suffix 'NN' indicating two nuts (e.g., 'Step Bolt M16 x 175 NN IS 10238').
Each step bolt must carry the manufacturer's identification mark and the property class (4.6) marked on the bolt head in accordance with IS 1367 (Part 3).

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Drums and Tins (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all 15 kg/litre Square Tins manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India for packaging ghee, vanaspati, edible oils, and bakery shortenings must conform to IS 10325:2000 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Enforcement transitioned for medium and large-scale enterprises on April 17, 2024, small enterprises on July 17, 2024, and micro enterprises on October 17, 2024. Manufacturing, importing, or distributing non-certified tins in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel/tin packaging.
requirements: Every certified square tin must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 10325) stenciled, printed, or embossed on the tin body or lid.
The tin coating must conform to Grade E 2.8/2.8 as evaluated by the chemical stripping method of IS 1327, ensuring a uniform protective barrier against corrosion.

The top and bottom end plates must be attached to the body using leak-proof double-seamed joints along with a food-grade seaming compound resistant to fats and oils. The side body seam must be securely welded (welded side seam) or folded and locked.
A carry handle manufactured from steel wire (diameter as specified) must be securely spot-welded or attached to the top end to withstand normal lifting and handling stresses without tearing free.

When intended for packing ghee specifically, the interior of the square tins must be coated with a compatible, non-toxic food-grade lacquer to prevent any off-flavors, rancidity, or chemical reaction.

To guarantee that the tins are completely leak-proof and can withstand handling pressures, representative sample tins must be subjected to an internal hydraulic pressure test of 30 kPa (0.30 kgf/cm²) for a period of not less than 3 minutes. The tins must show zero signs of leakage, sweating, or joint warping.
The interior of each finished square tin must be completely clean, dry, bright, and free from any traces of rust, solder flux, scale, or foreign contaminants before filling.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all high-strength structural nuts manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must conform to IS 6623 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified structural fasteners is a legal offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy-duty high-tensile steel fasteners.
requirements: Every structural nut or its packaging box must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance.

Nuts must be supplied in designated property classes 8S or 10S (conforming to IS 1367 Part 6). Class 8S nuts are specified for property class 8.8S structural bolts, and Class 10S nuts are specified for property class 10.9S structural bolts to ensure that thread stripping does not occur during tightening.

The proof load capacity of the nut must be designed to be greater than the ultimate tensile strength of its matching bolt. This ensures that in case of overload, the bolt will fail in tension (a ductile, predictable failure) rather than the nut stripping its threads (which causes sudden, catastrophic joint release).
The nut threads must be ISO Metric coarse pitch conforming to IS 4218, and must be manufactured to a strict tolerance class of 6H to ensure consistent thread engagement and ease of assembly.
The standard covers a diameter range of M16 to M36. The standard thread pitches are: M16 (2.0 mm), M20 (2.5 mm), M22 (2.5 mm), M24 (3.0 mm), M27 (3.0 mm), M30 (3.5 mm), and M36 (4.0 mm).
Under Table 1, the width across flats dimension for size M22 (Sl No. ix, Col 6) must comply with a maximum value of 36.0 mm and a minimum value of 35.0 mm [1].

The height of the nut (h) must be controlled to prevent thread failure: M16 (16.40 to 17.10 mm), M20 (19.40 to 20.70 mm), M22 (22.30 to 23.60 mm), M24 (22.90 to 24.20 mm), M27 (26.30 to 27.60 mm), M30 (29.10 to 30.70 mm), and M36 (35.00 to 36.60 mm).

Nuts can be supplied in three standard finishes depending on environmental exposure: dull black (self-colored), electroplated zinc, or hot-dip galvanized. Hot-dip galvanized nuts require overtapped threads to clear the zinc thickness, and must be lubricated with a suitable clean dry lubricant.

High-strength structural nuts must be marked with the property class designation (8S or 10S) and the manufacturer's identification symbol stamped or embossed on the non-bearing face of the nut to allow visual site verification.
